issue.title: Why rx throws OnErrorNotImplementedException when I have doOnError

CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is about understanding the behavior of RxJava's error handling mechanism, specifically why an OnErrorNotImplementedException is thrown despite having a doOnError handler. This is a conceptual issue that can be verified without a build environment. The problem is that the user is calling .subscribe() without providing an onError handler in the subscribe method, while assuming doOnError would handle the error completely. In RxJava, doOnError only observes errors but doesn't consume them - errors still propagate to subscribers. The solution would be to add an error handler in the subscribe method like .subscribe(onNext, onError). This is a common RxJava pattern that can be verified through documentation and code analysis without needing to build or run the code. The behavior is well-documented in RxJava's documentation and is a fundamental aspect of how the library works.
